name: Brassie
imitates: A slim midge larva; a simple copper-wire nymph that works year-round on tailwaters when midges dominate.

steps.text: Seat a curved scud hook in the vise.
Wrap lead wire over about a third of the shank, leaving a gap behind the eye.
Lock the thread behind the lead and build a smooth thread base over the wire and shank.
Tie in copper wire with its tip reaching forward to where the thorax ends, then wrap it in touching turns to form the abdomen.
Tie in two or three peacock herls with tips aligned, just in front of the abdomen, then advance the thread to behind the eye.
Wrap the herl forward for the thorax, pull back any forward-pointing fibers, and make a small head with a few quick wraps and a whip finish. The finished fly.
